comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: Operator framing 2026-07-28 (2nd): the meta-harness today harnesses Claude Code CLI specifically, but can/will expand to GitHub Copilot and perhaps more. Design consequence — a PORTABILITY GRADIENT inversely correlated with the enforcement-grade ladder: grades 1-3 (convention/git-friction/CI-backed-block) are substrate-AGNOSTIC (git+CI+crosslink are universal); grade 4 (harness-level capability restriction, e.g. Claude Code sub-agent tool-restriction / dispatch withholding) is substrate-SPECIFIC. So the STRONGEST enforcement is the LEAST portable. Architectural discipline this implies (fold into the post-verify revision, NOT a new build now — one harness today, abstracting for a second is premature): keep the vsdd CORE (integrity queries, gates over git/CI, tracker integration, pure derivation) harness-agnostic; concentrate substrate-specifics (statusline wiring, hooks, dispatch/capability) behind the per-harness adapter the supplements+vehicle concept already provides (supplements/claude-code-cli.md today; a copilot supplement later). Mark the draft's seam family accordingly: git+CI = portable; chassis session-start/pre-tool hooks + dispatch = adapter-provided. The core/adapter boundary is hard-to-undo, so getting it harness-agnostic now is cheap; retrofitting later is expensive. Reinforces the deflate+CI decision: CI (grade 3) is the portable strong backbone; grade-4 degrades to grade-3 on a harness that lacks the primitive.
